title: Regrouping and Theo's Camping Trip
goal: I can add and subtract with regrouping. I can tell what happens first, next, then and last in a story.

card.desc: Ce'Line learns to regroup: she carries when a column adds up to 10 or more, and she borrows when the top digit is too small to subtract, one column at a time, ones first (even across a zero, like 405 − 168). Then she follows Theo's overnight camping trip and puts the story in sequence: beginning, middle and end, and the transition words first, next, then and last. This gets her ready for the Pathways Week 3 Math and Reading retakes.

win: You carried, you borrowed, and you put Theo's camping trip in order. Great work, Ce'Line!

slides.title: Regrouping and Theo's Camping Trip
slides.text: Today you learn to carry and to borrow. Then you go camping with Theo! ⛺

notes.do: Before class (library table): base-ten pieces (real blocks, or paper ones cut from grid paper: 5 hundred flats, 20 ten strips, 20 ones), a place-value mat (a sheet of paper with three columns: H, T, O), whiteboard and marker, pencil and scrap paper, 3 index cards (BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END), 4 sticky notes (First, Next, Then, Last), and the printed Packet for her to take home.
notes.say: Today has two parts. First, math: adding and subtracting big numbers when a column needs help. Then reading: Theo goes camping, and we put his trip in order.
notes.ask: How are you feeling about math today, from 1 to 5?
notes.listen: Any answer is fine. If she says 1 or 2, tell her: today we go one column at a time, and I will do the first ones with you.

slides.title: Theo's next trip
slides.text: Last week, Theo used his compass to find the right trail. This week, Theo goes camping overnight.
prompts: Have you ever camped or slept outside? What would you bring?
When you get to a campsite, what should you do first? Why first?
Which camp job do you think comes before dinner? Why?
starters: Before dinner, they need to … because …

notes.do: 5 minutes, talk only. Tap the gold button for each full-sentence answer.
notes.say: Order matters when you camp. Order matters in a story too. That is our reading skill today.
notes.ask: Which has to come first at camp, the fire or the hot food? Why?
notes.listen: The fire, because there is nothing to cook on without it. Praise any answer with "because".

slides.title: Weeks 1 and 2
slides.text: Quick review of the last two weeks.

items.why: 278 is between 270 and 280. The ones digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so round up to 280.
items.no: Look at the ones digit. Is it 5 or more?

items.why: Hundreds are the same (7 and 7). Tens: 3 is less than 6. So 736 < 763.
items.no: Hundreds are the same. Now look at the tens.

items.q: A story takes place at a beach on a hot morning. The beach and the morning are the …
items.why: Where and when a story happens is the setting.
no: Characters are the people or animals in a story.
The conflict is the problem in the story.

items.q: Theo could not find the trail sign. That problem is the story's ____.
items.why: A problem in a story is the conflict. Theo's conflict was the missing trail sign.
items.no: It is a Week 2 word. It starts with c.

notes.do: She answers out loud first, then taps or types. 4 minutes.
notes.ask: How did you know to round 278 up?
notes.listen: 280 (8 is 5 or more), <, setting, conflict. If she misses one, say the rule once and move on. We review again next week.

slides.title: Math words for today
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Read the word and the meaning out loud.

words.meaning: To trade 10 of one place for 1 of the next place.
words.example: 10 ones = 1 ten. I regroup 10 ones as 1 ten.

words.meaning: To move a regrouped ten (or hundred) to the next column when you add.
To take 1 ten from the next column so you have 10 more ones to subtract.
words.example: In 42 − 8, 2 is too small. I borrow 1 ten.

notes.do: She reads each card aloud, then covers it and says the meaning in her own words.
notes.say: Pathways asks you to TYPE these words, so we say them and spell them today. The word is regroup, not regrouping.
notes.ask: Which word is the answer to an adding problem? Which is the answer to a subtracting problem?
notes.listen: Sum for adding, difference for subtracting. Carry goes with adding; borrow goes with subtracting.

slides.title: Trade 10 for 1
slides.text: In each place, you can only have 0 to 9. When you get 10 or more, you trade.

steps.text: You have 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place.
Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Now you have 1 ten and 4 ones.
You have 12 tens. Trade 10 tens for 1 hundred. Now you have 1 hundred and 2 tens.
When you make this trade, you regroup. Adding and subtracting use it all the time.

slides.tip: Only 0 to 9 can live in one place. 10 or more? Trade!

notes.do: Hands-on: she counts out 14 ones on the mat, then trades 10 of them for 1 ten strip. Then 12 ten strips: she trades 10 for 1 hundred flat.
notes.say: Ten ones and one ten are the same amount. We just make it neat.
notes.ask: If you have 17 ones, how many tens and ones after you trade? If you have 11 tens?
notes.listen: 17 ones = 1 ten and 7 ones. 11 tens = 1 hundred and 1 ten. If she says 17 tens, put the pieces in her hand and count again.

visual.text:
The Beginning
“Dad, can we camp overnight this time?” Theo asked, spreading the trail map across the kitchen table. His father grinned. “I was hoping you'd ask.” They packed the tent, the sleeping bags, and a box of matches. Theo's little sister Mia begged to come too, and this time, their parents said yes.

slides.text: Look for the transition words.

visual.text:
The Middle
FIRST, they found a flat clearing near the stream and pitched the tent, hammering each stake into the ground. NEXT, Theo gathered dry branches while Dad built a ring of stones for the fire. THEN, once the fire crackled to life, Mia helped stir a pot of chili bubbling over the flames.

items.no: Look at the start of the second sentence.

no: They hammered stakes for the tent. Branches were for something else.

items.q: How many transition words are in this part? Type a number.
items.why: FIRST, NEXT and THEN. That is 3.
items.no: Look for the big capital words.

slides.title: The end
slides.text: How does the story wrap up?

visual.text:
The End
LAST, after the dishes were washed in the stream, the family lay back on a blanket and looked up. The sky above the campsite had no city lights to compete with, just thousands of stars, more than Theo had ever counted. Mia fell asleep first, her head on Dad's shoulder. Theo stayed awake a little longer, thinking that some things, like counting stars with your family, are worth staying up for.

teacher.objective: Math (28 min): Ce'Line adds 2- and 3-digit numbers with regrouping (carrying once and twice, ones first, right to left) and subtracts with regrouping (borrowing once and twice, and across a zero, as in 405 − 168), checks a subtraction by adding back, and finds the two classic mistakes (flipping 2 − 7 to 7 − 2, and forgetting the carried 1). Reading (18 min): she reads Theo's overnight camping story from Pathways Week 3 Reading, tells what the beginning, middle and end do, finds the transition words first, next, then and last, and puts the events in sequence. This is everything on the Pathways Week 3 Math and Reading retakes.
materials: The class lesson on a laptop or tablet (teacher code 9110)

Base-ten pieces: 5 hundred flats, 20 ten strips, 20 ones (real blocks, or paper ones cut from grid paper). The most used at one time is 405 − 168 on slide 12 (4 flats and 5 ones, then a flat traded for 10 strips)
A place-value mat: one sheet of paper with three columns labeled H, T, O
Whiteboard and marker; pencil and scrap paper; a red pencil (or she circles) for carried and borrowed digits
3 index cards (BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END) and 4 sticky notes (First, Next, Then, Last)

watch: Flipping to subtract: in 362 − 147 she may do 7 − 2 = 5 in the ones and get 225. Say: "The top number is what we have. Is 2 big enough to take away 7? No, so we borrow."
Forgetting the carried 1: 259 + 168 = 417 instead of 427. Have her write the 1 in red at the top of the next column before she adds that column.
Writing 15 in one place: 3615-type answers mean she wrote the whole sum in the ones place. Go back to the pieces: only 0 to 9 fit in one place.
Not lowering the lender: 352 − 127 = 235 means she borrowed but did not change the 5 tens to 4. Every borrow is two marks: cross out and write one less, then add 10 to the ones.
Across a zero: for 405 − 168 or 300 − 146, the 0 tens become 10 and then 9. 247 or 164 means she left the tens at 10. Pathways Week 3 Math has this in the Boss Battle ($500 − $235).

Pathways Week 3 Math typed answers must be exact: it accepts only regroup (not regrouping), borrow, carry, sum, difference, ones (start column), ten (10 ones are traded for 1 what?), right to left, 1 less (what happens to the tens digit when it lends) and yes / no. Tell her before she starts.

Pathways Week 3 Reading typed answers must be exact too: the three transition words in the middle are typed first, next, then; the beginning sets up "who is in it and what is about to happen" (it wants the whole phrase "who is in it and what is about to happen"); a good ending wraps up the feeling; Theo feels grateful; and "words like first, next, then and last are called ___ words" is transition. Names are typed as one word: mia, dad, stream, stones, chili, map, overnight, stars.
